Key fields26ATo distinguish between records in a database table, there must be key fields. Different types of key fields serve for different purposes.

Key fields27AA candidate key is a key field that always stores unique data for every record. Therefore, a candidate key can be used to identify records.In the above table, the field SID stores unique data for every record. Therefore, it is a candidate key for the table STUDENT

Key fields28ASometimes, a candidate key may consist of more than one field. This type of candidate key is called composite key.In the table STUDENT, CLASS+CNO is a composite key since it is impossible for two students to share the same class and the same class number at the same time.

Key fields29AA composite key must be minimal, meaning that the removal of any field within the key results in duplicated values.CLASS+CNO is a composite key as the removal of either CLASS or CNO results in duplicated values.
Concept of a Relational Database34.1The elements of a relational database are usually stored as or represented by different elements in a Database Management System (DBMS).

Key fields31AThe primary key of a table must be one of the candidate keys of that table. It is a candidate key chosen by the database administrator to identify records. A table can have multiple candidate keys, but it can have one primary key only.
Key fields32ABelow is the table structure of STUDENT:For the table STUDENT, we have three candidate keys: SID, EMAIL and CLASS+CNO.
Key fields33AHowever, only one of them can be the primary key of the table STUDENT.

Key fields34AEMAIL is not the best primary key as a student may change their personal email address for reasons such as forgetting the password of the email address and the deactivation of the email address. Which one, SID or CLASS+CNO, would you choose to be the primary key? Explain briefly.SID, as the CLASS+CNO of a student usually changes every year while SID does not.

Key fields35AForeign keys are used to show the relationship between records in two tables. A foreign key in a table X is always the primary key of another table Y.In such case, table X is referred to as the host table and table Y is referred to as the parent table.
Key fields36AThe CID field in table STUDENT is a foreign key that links the host table STUDENT to the parent table CLUB.

Key fields37AUsing a foreign key allows us to manage the data better. For example:When the name, room or teacher of a club is updated in the table CLUB, we do not have to update the table STUDENT as STUDENT stores the identity code of a club only; andEven if the records of all students who join a certain club are deleted in table STUDENT, the data of this club will be kept in table CLUB.

Key fields38AImagine the data of students and clubs are stored in the same table.If the teacher of Science Club is changed from Mr Wong to Mr Suen, three records needs to be updated or the data will be inconsistent; andIf the only student in Art Club, i.e. Ada, quits the school, the data of Art Club will be lost.

Index47BWhen a field is expected to be searched frequently, we can index that field to speed up the data retrieval process.Indexing a field creates an index table containing the indexed field and a pointer to the related records only.

Index48BHowever, the DBMS needs to update the index table if changes are made to the data in the indexed field or a new record is added.It takes time for the DBMS to update and storage space to store the index table. Therefore, it is wise to index a field only if necessary.

Entity5AAn entity type is a collection of entities sharing similar attributes. For example, a specific student can be an entity and a collection of students from the same school is an entity type.

Integrity504.3When we update the data in a DBMS, the integrity of data may be affected, meaning that the data is no longer accurate or valid. Here are three aspects of integrity that we should pay attention to:Entity integrityReferential integrityDomain integrity

Entity integrity51AEntity integrity means that: a table must have its primary key defined; andthe primary key for each record is unique and not NULL. When using a DBMS, it is important to define a primary key for a table.Once the primary key is defined, the DBMS will ensure that the primary key for each record is unique and not NULL.

Entity integrity52ASee the following table:If SID is set as the primary key, you will NOT be able to:insert a new record with an SID of 03493 or update a record to have an SID of 03493 since this SID is already occupied by the student Ada; orinsert a new record without SID since the primary key for a record cannot be NULL.
Entity integrity53AA table violates entity integrity if:it does not have a primary key;its primary key contains duplicated values; orits primary key contains a NULL value.

Referential integrity54BReferential integrity means that the references of foreign keys in a table are valid so that its relationship with other tables remains intact.Once the foreign key is defined, the DBMS will ensure that the values of foreign key for each record must come from the values of the field it references. It does not stop a record to have NULL as the value of a foreign key though.
Referential integrity55BSee the following tables:
Referential integrity56BAssume that CLUB.CID is the primary key of the table CLUB and STUDENT.CID is the foreign key of the table STUDENT which links to CLUB.CID.
Referential integrity57BExcluding NULL values, each foreign key value (CID) in the host table (STUDENT) must come from the primary key value (CID) in the parent table (CLUB).

Referential integrity58BThus, the DBMS prevents actions that would cause a foreign key value (CID) in the host table (STUDENT) to reference a primary key value (CID) that does not exist in the parent table. It means you will NOT be able to:
Referential integrity59BInsert a new record into STUDENT with a CID that does not exist in CLUB;
Entity6AIn the table below, students are an entity type and a single student (e.g. Ada) is an entity
Referential integrity60BUpdate a record in STUDENT to have a CID that does not exist in CLUB;
Referential integrity61BDelete a record from CLUB with a CID that is referenced by STUDENT; and
Referential integrity62BUpdate the CID of a record in CLUB that is referenced by STUDENT to a new value.

Domain integrity63CDomain integrity means that the value of an attribute must fall within a reasonable domain.When using a DBMS, we may define the domain of an attribute by setting its data type and constraints.
Domain integrity64CSee the following table:

Domain integrity65CCREATE TABLE STUDENT (	SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY,	NAME VARCHAR(40),	SEX CHAR(1),	CLASS CHAR(2),	CNO INT,	CHECK (LENGTH(SID) = 5),	CHECK (SEX IN ('M', 'F')),	CHECK (CLASS IN ('1A', '1B', '1C', '1D')),	CHECK (CNO BETWEEN 1 AND 30))

Domain integrity66CIf the data types and constraints of the mentioned attributes are defined as above, you will NOT be able to:insert a new record with an SID of less than 5 characters; orupdate a record to have a CLASS other than 1A, 1B, 1C and 1D; orinsert a new record with a CNO of One; orupdate a record to have a CNO of –6.A table violates domain integrity if its field contains a value that is not within its domain.

Attribute7BAn attribute is the property of an entity. An entity can have multiple attributes.In the table STUDENT mentioned in the previous section, the name (NAME) and the sex (SEX) of a student are attributes of the entity type, students (STUDENT).

Rollback704.4A rollback means restoring a database to its previous state. When managing a database, errors may occur and corrupt the integrity of data. Therefore, we must make a backup of our database regularly. When needed, we can roll back our database using the backup.
Rollback714.4See the following table:A new school year is coming soon, a teacher wants to: 1. delete students in class 6A; and 2. promote all students in class 5A to class 6A.

Rollback724.4It means two SQL statements are needed:DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '6A'UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS = '6A' WHERE CLASS = '5A‘However, they mess up the order of operations. Now all 5A students are promoted to 6A, then all 6A students are deleted, leaving the table empty. This is where we need a rollback.
